_comment: Input for writing creatives. Record angles and patterns, never copy a competitor's wording or footage. Spend figures are AdKit's rough estimates. Founder-reported results are unverified.

competitors.name: Unhook
competitors.focus: Hides YouTube UI such as recommendations and Shorts

competitors.name: PhobiaBlocker
competitors.focus: Hides spider and insect images in the browser
competitors.gap: Store reviews mention slow blocking and false positives such as Spider-Man

angles.audience: Anyone who's felt awkward watching a scene with a partner or parents
angles.pain: Uncomfortable scenes turn up in almost every movie: sexualized scenes, cringe romantic scenes, and anything awkward to watch with a partner or parents. The founder kept having to look away, and built unscene.it because of it.
angles.language: That scene comes on while you're watching with your parents
angles.source: The founder, Nov 5, 2026. True story: only the founder tells it in the first person. Unscene.it has no dedicated filter for cringe romantic scenes, so don't promise one.

angles.language: One viewer blocks only spiders; another blocks gore and anything over 12

angles.pain: Hovering over the remote when watching with kids
angles.language: How to stop YouTube showing scary thumbnails to toddlers

angles.pain: Unexpected spiders in videos and thumbnails
angles.language: Extension to hide spiders on YouTube thumbnails

angles.pain: Wanting the story without the graphic scenes
angles.language: Trigger warning extension for blood and gore

angles.pain: Subtle content that most filters ignore

angles.audience: Viewers of videos outside the library
angles.pain: The video they want isn't screened yet
angles.language: Not in the library? Xenia screens it live.

ads_reviewed.relevance: Adjacent: consumer screen-time app, not a direct competitor. About $120-241k estimated spend, 321 active ads.
ads_reviewed.pattern: Two founders on camera, phone-shot, 99s. Text box names the problem and who it's for, with word-by-word captions. Family story: a mother's phone addiction, 'nothing was working', so they built something.
ads_reviewed.why_it_might_work: A specific person's problem, told by the people who built the fix. No app UI in the sampled frames.

ads_reviewed.pattern: Founder at a table, then cuts of daily life with a Bible. A faith-specific version: the phone pulling him away from God, so he built something. 104s.
ads_reviewed.why_it_might_work: Same product, retold for one community with a strong identity. Relevant to viewers who prefer modest content, if told honestly.

ads_reviewed.pattern: Founders hold handwritten cards and drop them one at a time: quit big tech jobs, Apple and Meta obstacles, nearly going under. 68s.
ads_reviewed.why_it_might_work: An underdog story with a visual device that's cheap to shoot and rewards watching to the next card.

ads_reviewed.relevance: Adjacent: distraction blocker that also ships a browser extension. About $284-640k estimated spend.
ads_reviewed.estimated_spend: $50-110k and $21-46k on the first two, under $1.1k on the third
ads_reviewed.pattern: Search ads built on the viewer's own problem and on control, running since 2024-2025.
ads_reviewed.why_it_might_work: Long-running with real spend. Useful for search wording, less so for short video.

organic_references.name: Opal
organic_references.lesson: Hired a TikTok creator who already used the app. Her own-name channels went from 0 to 700,000 followers across platforms in a few months, per the founder. An organic video of hers reached tens of millions and then ran as an ad.

organic_references.name: Tactiq
organic_references.lesson: Chrome extension reported 150,000+ users from about $1,820 paid to TikTok creators, after contacting 320 of them. Founder-reported, and only read through a search summary because the original page blocked access.

organic_references.name: Does The Dog Die
organic_references.lesson: Closest cousin to the product's idea. Grew slowly, then broke out through press and community sites in 2013, including a Slate mention in a piece on trigger warnings and a MetaFilter front page.
